questions.question: Charge is quantised. This means:
options: Charge exists only in whole-number multiples of the electron's charge, 1,6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C
Charge can take any value at all

questions.question: A sphere carries −8 × 10⁻¹⁸ C. The number of excess electrons on it is:
options: 50 — n = (8 × 10⁻¹⁸) ÷ (1,6 × 10⁻¹⁹), a pure count with no unit

questions.question: An object that has LOST 2,5 × 10¹¹ electrons carries a charge of:
options: +4 × 10⁻⁸ C — losing electrons leaves a proton surplus, so the sign is positive

questions.question: One nanocoulomb equals:

subtopics.title: Three Ways to Charge an Object

questions.question: In every charging process, the particles that move are:
options: Electrons only — protons stay locked in their nuclei

questions.question: A plastic ruler rubbed through a woollen sleeve becomes negative because:
options: The ruler lost protons to the sleeve
The sleeve absorbed the ruler's positive charge
The ruler grips electrons more strongly and stripped them from the wool

questions.question: Charging by contact leaves the two conductors with:
options: The same sign of charge — the surplus electrons spread across both
Charge only on the larger one

questions.question: In charging by induction with a negative rod, the sphere ends up positive because:
options: The rod's electrons jumped onto the sphere
The rod removed protons from the sphere
Repelled electrons drained to earth through the finger, and rod and finger were removed in the right order
The sphere was rubbed by the rod

subtopics.title: Conservation of Charge and the Sharing Rule

questions.question: The principle of conservation of charge states that charge:
options: Cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred
Is created whenever objects are rubbed

questions.question: Identical spheres P (−5 nC) and R (+1 nC) touch and separate. Each carries:
Sphere P went from −5 nC to −2 nC in that contact. The number of electrons it passed to R is:
Adding the sizes of +5 nC and −1 nC to get 3 nC each after contact is wrong because:
options: It creates charge from nowhere — the signed total must be conserved
The halving rule applies only to insulators

subtopics.title: Coulomb's Law and the Inverse Square

questions.question: Coulomb's law states that the force between two point charges is:
options: Proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance
Proportional to the sum of the charges and the distance
Inversely proportional to the product of the charges

questions.question: Charges of +2 × 10⁻⁶ C and −6 × 10⁻⁶ C sit 0,20 m apart. The force between them is:
The same charges are moved to 0,40 m apart. The force becomes:
options: 0,675 N — a quarter, because the distance is squared

questions.question: Substituting r = 20 instead of r = 0,20 m into Coulomb's law makes the answer wrong by a factor of:
options: Ten thousand — the centimetre error is squared along with r

subtopics.title: The Balloon and the School Jersey

questions.question: After the balloon is rubbed on the jersey:
options: The balloon is negative with extra electrons; the jersey is positive, having lost them
The balloon is positive; the jersey gained protons

questions.question: The unrubbed wall holds the balloon because:
options: The balloon's electrons push the wall's electrons back, leaving the wall's face slightly positive
The paint is sticky at small scales
The balloon is lighter than air

questions.question: Charge comes only in whole steps because:
options: Only whole electrons can move — never half of one

subtopics.title: Three Ways to Get Charged, and Sharing the Total

questions.question: The winter gate-latch shock happens because:
options: The latch is naturally charged in winter
The latch is warmer than your hand
You harvested electrons crossing the carpet, and the metal latch is their first escape route

questions.question: Touching a negative rod to a neutral metal ball leaves the ball:
options: Negative — contact shares the same sign

questions.question: In induction, the finger must be removed BEFORE the rod because otherwise:
options: The rod would lose its own charge
The escaped electrons would simply return through the finger and the ball would end neutral
The ball would explode with charge

questions.question: Identical balls holding −5 and +1 touch and separate. Each ends with:
options: −2 — pool with signs to −4, then split evenly

questions.question: Doubling the distance between two charges changes the force to:
options: A quarter — the distance is squared, so it bites twice

questions.question: Two millionths and six millionths of a coulomb sit 0,20 m apart. The force is:
Centimetres must become metres BEFORE substituting into Coulomb's law because:
options: Centimetres are not allowed in physics
The constant k only likes small numbers
The distance is about to be squared, so the slip multiplies to ten thousand times

questions.question: The minus signs on charges are kept out of the Coulomb calculation because:
options: Signs make the force too large
The formula gives the size; attraction or repulsion is then stated in words
